source.title: Unlocking In-Context Learning for Natural Datasets Beyond Language Modelling
source.authors: Jelena Bratulić; Sudhanshu Mittal; David T. Hoffmann; Samuel Böhm; R. Schirrmeister; Tonio Ball; Christian Rupprecht; T. Brox

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or corruption; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests induction-like mechanisms and how training conditions affect in-context classification, using visual and EEG tasks and attention-progress measures rather than language-modeling measurements from the original work.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own ICL accuracy results, training-time attention measures, and EEG classification results. The training-corpus n-gram repetition counts in Figure 10 are also reported, but are not rows because they measure corpus statistics rather than model induction behavior. Results cited from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: It trains GPT-2 models from scratch on image-label and EEG-label sequences. It tracks previous-token-head formation and query-to-label retrieval attention (Fig. 5, Fig. 13) and reports how exact copies, class count, label swapping, skew and the IWL objective change ICL. This is a new modality setting with its own results on V1, V4 and V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim burstiness is not essential and that a single exact copy can suffice. The Fig. 12 caption contradicts this, and its own wording is inconsistent.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains GPT-2-based models from scratch on interleaved image-label or EEG-label sequences and measures few-shot classification and attention progress metrics, rather than testing language-model token-copy behavior. It varies exact instance copies, burstiness, label swapping, and IWL difficulty.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with exact instance copies, burstiness, training-class count, label swapping, data skew, IWL objective, image embedder design, and (in EEG experiments) held-out dataset and training choices. The main text and supplementary material conflict on whether a single exact copy is sufficient.
record.code_released: https://github.com/jelenab98/unlocking icl (as printed in the text)
record.peer_reviewed: DAGM GCPR (2025; stated in the supplied study metadata)
record.problems: Several attention and accuracy trajectories are presented only as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The paper reports averages over three seeds but gives no error bars or confidence intervals in the supplied text. It uses GPT-2-based models only, and the supplementary material conflicts with the main text on whether a single exact copy suffices.

untested.parts: Attention-only transformers and language-token copying. Composition (K/Q-composition) between the layers is not tested directly; only attention progress metrics are reported.
All of it. Abruptness, the narrow window, and coincidence with an ICL gain or a loss bump are not analysed.
All of it. Large language models are not studied.
Other model families, sizes, training runs and non-transformer architectures. Induction heads are measured only on Omniglot, not on CIFAR, Caltech, DTD or EEG.
Language-model training data, and the timing of formation beyond the training plots.

missing.what: Pretrained ResNet-18 embedder makes IWL converge fast and ICL fails to emerge, unlike a from-scratch embedder
Higher burstiness levels (3xQ-3xA-B-C vs Q-A-...-G) give better ICL, with IWL similar at convergence
Longer learning-rate warm-up stated to enhance ICL performance
Bursty-only model shows high image-image query (similarity matching) attention; this metric rises in the instCopy model as its ICL becomes transient

record.verdict_notes: Models are GPT-2 with MLPs and a ResNet or D4 embedder, not attention-only. Induction-head evidence comes only from Omniglot attention metrics, mostly shown as figures. The vision and EEG results are ICL accuracy only, so they bear on V5, not on head universality (V4). Results are averaged over 3 seeds with no error bars. Tranche set to T3 (new modality setting) rather than T2.

versions.untested_parts: The tests concern image-label and EEG-label classification, not language-token copying. The analyzed models are not stated to be attention-only transformers.
The paper plots training trajectories, but does not establish that formation is abrupt in a narrow window, that it coincides with a sharp ICL gain, or that either coincides with a training-loss bump.
No test of whether induction heads carry most ICL in large language transformers.
The study tests visual and EEG settings using GPT-2-based models; it does not test other model families or non-transformer architectures.
The tested data and training changes are within the paper's classification setups; it does not test language-model training data or whether ICL persists in language models.
The paper does not compare induction heads against other mechanisms as the main carrier of few-shot task learning.
Although it tracks multiple attention progress measures, it does not test whether induction-head formation consists of multiple distinct transitions rather than one transition.
